# P2P File

> P2P File sends a file straight from one browser to another using a
> one-time passphrase. Peer-to-peer over WebRTC; the file itself is never
> uploaded to a server or stored.

The whole tool is one page. Pick a file, get a three-word passphrase, and
share it however you like. The other person opens this same page, types the
passphrase in, and accepts the file.

## How it works

- The sender picks a file and gets a passphrase like "correct-horse-battery".
- The receiver types the passphrase into the same site and accepts the
  transfer.
- The file streams directly between the two browsers over a WebRTC data
  channel, encrypted end-to-end with DTLS.
- The server only relays the small handshake messages the two browsers need
  to find each other. The file itself never touches the server.

## Limits

- Each passphrase works once, then it is gone. It also dies if the sender
  closes their tab, or after a few minutes if nobody claims it.
- Desktop Chrome, Edge and Brave save the file to disk as it arrives, so
  transfers up to 16GB are allowed. Firefox, Safari and mobile browsers must
  hold the file in memory first, so they are capped at 250MB.
- Both browser tabs must stay open for the whole transfer. There is no
  resume if either side closes early.

## Cost and account

- Free. No account, no sign-up, no upload limit tracking.
